name: Kanji Vada
blurb: Moong dal vadas soaked in a sour mustard water that ferments for two days. Made for Holi.

steps.text: Grind the mustard seeds coarsely and stir them with chilli powder, hing, kala namak and salt into boiled, cooled water. Leave in a jar in the sun for two days.
Soak the dal four hours and grind it thick; whisk until light.
Fry small vadas, then soak them in warm water for ten minutes and squeeze.
Drop the vadas into the kanji and leave for a few hours before serving.

name: Muthia
blurb: Steamed rolls of flour and grated vegetables, sliced and tempered with sesame.

steps.text: Mix the flours, grated gourd, ginger, chillies, yogurt, spices, sugar, soda, salt and a spoon of oil into a soft dough.
Shape into logs and steam for 20 minutes. Cool and slice.
Crackle the mustard, sesame and hing in oil.
Toss the slices in it until crisp at the edges.

name: Handvo
blurb: Savoury rice and lentil cake with bottle gourd, baked or cooked in a pan with a sesame crust.

steps.text: Soak the rice and dals six hours, grind coarse with yogurt and ferment overnight.
Mix in the gourd, ginger, chillies, turmeric and salt; add the Eno just before cooking.
Crackle the mustard, sesame and hing in oil in a heavy pan; pour in the batter.
Cover and cook on low until set and crusty underneath, then flip and cook the other side.

name: Methi Na Gota
blurb: Dakor's fluffy fenugreek fritters with crushed pepper and coriander.

steps.text: Mix the besan, sooji, chopped methi, crushed pepper and coriander, ginger, chillies, mashed banana, sugar and salt.
Add water to make a thick batter and rest ten minutes.
Stir in the soda and a spoon of hot oil.
Drop small balls into hot oil and fry until golden.

name: Fafda
blurb: Crisp besan strips with ajwain, pressed out by hand. Gujarat's Sunday breakfast with jalebi.

steps.text: Knead the besan with ajwain, turmeric, soda, salt, oil and water into a smooth, soft dough.
Rest ten minutes, then knead again with oiled hands.
Press a small ball along a wooden board with the heel of your palm into a long thin strip; lift it with a knife.
Fry until crisp. Fry the green chillies too. Sprinkle pepper.

name: Khichu
blurb: Soft rice flour dough cooked with cumin and chilli, eaten hot with oil and pickle masala.

steps.text: Boil 2½ cups of water with cumin, ajwain, chillies, soda and salt.
Lower the heat and stir in the rice flour with a rolling pin handle until no lumps remain.
Cover and steam on low for ten minutes.
Serve hot drizzled with oil and achar masala.

name: Sev Khamani
blurb: Surat's crumbled chana dal khaman, tempered and topped with sev and pomegranate.

steps.text: Soak the dal four hours; grind coarse with ginger and chillies.
Add turmeric, salt and Eno; steam for 15 minutes. Cool and crumble.
Temper the mustard, sesame and hing; pour over with sugar, lemon and a little water.
Top with sev, pomegranate and coriander.

name: Patra
blurb: Colocasia leaves spread with sweet-sour besan paste, rolled, steamed and sliced.

steps.text: Make a thick paste of besan, tamarind water, jaggery, ginger, the powders and salt.
Lay a leaf vein side up, spread the paste, add another leaf and repeat. Fold the sides in and roll tightly.
Steam the rolls for 25 minutes. Cool and slice.
Temper the mustard and sesame; toss the slices in it.

name: Poha Chivda
blurb: Thin poha roasted crisp with peanuts, curry leaves and a little sugar. Keeps for weeks in a jar.

steps.text: Dry roast the thin poha on low until crisp.
Fry the peanuts, chana, cashews, raisins, mustard, hing, chillies and curry leaves in oil.
Add the turmeric and chilli powder, then the poha, sugar and salt; toss well.
Cool completely before storing.

name: Kothimbir Vadi
blurb: Steamed and fried coriander and besan squares from Maharashtra.

steps.text: Mix the chopped coriander, besan, rice flour, sesame, spices, crushed ginger, garlic, chillies and salt with a little water into a thick dough.
Press into a greased tray and steam for 20 minutes.
Cool and cut into squares.
Shallow fry until crisp on both sides.

name: Bhakarwadi
blurb: Pune's spiral snack: crisp dough rolled with a sweet, hot coconut and sesame filling.

steps.text: Knead the maida, besan, salt and oil with water into a stiff dough; rest 20 minutes.
Roast the coconut, sesame, poppy and fennel; crush with the powders, sugar and salt.
Roll the dough thin, brush with water, spread the filling and roll tightly into a log. Cut into small pieces and press each lightly.
Fry on low heat until crisp and golden.

name: Veg Frankie
blurb: Mumbai's wrap of spiced potato, onion and chutney in a soft flatbread.

steps.text: Knead the flours with salt and water into a soft dough; roll and cook thin rotis lightly.
Mash the boiled potatoes with the powders and shape into logs; pan-fry until crisp.
Soak the sliced onion in vinegar with chilli powder.
Spread chutney on a roti, add the potato, onion and capsicum, sprinkle chaat masala and roll up.

name: Bombay Sandwich
blurb: Bread with green chutney, sliced vegetables and sandwich masala, grilled or not.

steps.text: Butter the bread and spread with green chutney.
Layer thin slices of potato, cucumber, tomato and onion.
Sprinkle chaat masala, cumin, pepper and salt between the layers.
Close and grill until crisp, or eat as it is.

name: Masala Pav
blurb: Pav split and tossed on the tawa in buttery pav bhaji masala, onion and tomato.

steps.text: Melt butter, fry the garlic, onion and capsicum, add the tomatoes and mash.
Add pav bhaji masala, chilli powder and salt; cook to a thick masala.
Slit the pav and press them into the masala on both sides.
Finish with lemon and coriander.

name: Chicken Lollipop
blurb: Frenched chicken wings in a hot red batter, fried crisp. An Indo-Chinese party starter.

steps.text: Push the meat down each wing bone to shape a lollipop.
Coat with ginger-garlic paste, soy, vinegar, chilli powder, pepper, Manchurian masala and salt. Rest 30 minutes.
Add the egg, cornflour and maida to make a sticky coating.
Fry until crisp and cooked through.

name: Chilli Paneer
blurb: Crisp paneer tossed with peppers, onion and chilli in a soy glaze.

steps.text: Coat the paneer cubes in cornflour, maida, chilli powder and salt with a little water; fry until crisp.
Fry the garlic and chillies on high heat; add the onion and capsicum.
Add soy, vinegar, ketchup and pepper; thicken with a spoon of cornflour in water.
Toss in the paneer and spring onions.

name: Veg Manchurian
blurb: Fried cabbage and carrot balls in a garlicky soy sauce.

steps.text: Mix the grated cabbage and carrot with half the cornflour, the maida, pepper and salt; shape small balls.
Fry the balls until crisp.
Fry the garlic, ginger and chillies on high; add soy, Manchurian masala and a cup of water.
Thicken with cornflour in water, add the balls and spring onions.

name: Honey Chilli Potato
blurb: Crisp potato fingers in a sticky sweet and hot glaze with sesame.

steps.text: Parboil the potato fingers for three minutes; drain and coat in cornflour, chilli powder and salt.
Fry until crisp.
Fry the garlic, add soy, ketchup and chilli flakes; take off the heat and stir in the honey.
Toss the potatoes, sesame and spring onions in the glaze.

name: Seekh Kebab
blurb: Spiced minced meat pressed onto skewers and grilled until charred.

steps.text: Squeeze the grated onion dry and mix with the mince, toasted besan, spices, herbs, chillies and salt. Knead well and chill 20 minutes.
Press around skewers with wet hands.
Grill or pan-cook, turning, and brush with butter until charred.
Sprinkle chaat masala.

name: Galouti Kebab
blurb: Lucknow's melt-in-the-mouth mutton kebab, minced very fine and pan-fried in ghee.

steps.text: Mix the mince with papaya paste and ginger-garlic paste; rest four hours in the fridge.
Grind the fried onions, cardamom, mace and saffron in milk; add with the toasted besan, spices and salt; mix until smooth as paste.
Shape small flat patties with wet hands.
Cook in ghee on low heat, two minutes a side.
